rationale: This unit introduces third-grade students to the foundational elements of the design process: understanding what makes a product 'good' (criteria), describing and selecting appropriate materials based on those criteria, building a physical representation (prototype), and assessing its effectiveness. The addition of a dedicated skill for describing material characteristics ensures students have the necessary foundational knowledge before making material selections.

rationale: This unit focuses on developing foundational skills in understanding and interacting with low-voltage electrical circuits. It emphasizes practical measurement using multimeters and the symbolic representation of circuits, which are critical for both analysis and design in technical systems. The inclusion of resistor color codes provides a complementary method for component identification. Safety is paramount, with a focus on low-voltage DC circuits and supervised activities. The skills are chosen to be atomic and durable, providing a strong base for future learning in electronics and engineering.
safety_notes: All circuit activities must use low-voltage DC power sources (e.g., batteries up to 9V). Students must be supervised at all times. Emphasize never connecting components directly to wall outlets. Instruct students to always disconnect power before making changes to a circuit or measuring resistance. Multimeters should be handled with care and set to the correct function before connecting to a circuit.
